dish_name: Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
instructions: Bring 4 quarts of water to a boil in a large pot over high heat.
Meanwhile, trim the tough ends off the broccoli rabe and cut the rest into 1 1/2 inch pieces. Mince the 4 garlic cloves. Finely grate the 2 oz pecorino. That should be about 1 cup.
Squeeze the 12 oz sausage out of its casings into a bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Add the 1/2 cup panko and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's golden and smells toasty. Transfer it to a small bowl.

Turn the heat up to medium high and add the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and the sausage. Break it into rough 1/2 inch pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's browned with crisp edges and there's no pink left.
Stir in the garlic and the 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant. Turn off the heat.

Add the 1 tbsp salt and the broccoli rabe to the boiling water. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring often, until it's bright green and crisp tender. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and add it to the skillet with the sausage.

Bring the water back to a boil and add the 12 oz orecchiette. Cook it for the time on the package, stirring often, until it's tender with a little bite. Scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water, then drain it.

Set the skillet over medium heat and add the orecchiette, 1/2 cup of the pecorino and 1/3 cup of the cooking water. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until the cheese melts and the orecchiette look glossy. If it looks dry, add a splash more of the cooking water.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Scatter the toasted panko, the rest of the pecorino and the 1/4 tsp pepper over the top and serve.
method_notes: All three blanch the broccoli rabe briefly in the pasta water, cook the pasta in that same water and bring everything together in a skillet of garlic, chili and olive oil with a splash of the starchy water. America's Test Kitchen browns sausage in a nonstick skillet, adds garlic and a little chili, blanches the rabe for 2 minutes and tosses it all with Pecorino and reserved water; its page gives 459 reviews (a reviewCount, no ratingCount), recorded as the rating count here. The Daily Meal version melts anchovy into the garlic oil, makes sausage optional and tops the pasta with fried breadcrumbs, and Love and Lemons adds lemon, wine, sun-dried tomatoes and pine nuts. This follows America's Test Kitchen with more sausage for a dinner for 4 and the toasted crumbs from The Daily Meal for crunch.
